row.evidence: GetAccept's pricing lists Single sign-on (SSO) under Enterprise ('Contact us'; an add-on on Professional), and its Okta SCIM guide says 'Okta requires the SSO to be set up to be able to set up the SCIM.'
row.notes: New in 2026-09. Plans: eSign $25/u/mo, Professional $49/u/mo (min 5 users, annual), Enterprise Contact us. No page states which plan includes SCIM; it is recorded as Enterprise because SCIM (at least via Okta) requires SSO, which is Enterprise-only or a paid add-on on Professional, so confidence is low. A Professional customer buying the SSO add-on may also be able to use SCIM. SCIM supports Okta (catalogue app) and Entra (non-gallery app with tenant URL and token): create, update, inactivate on delete, teams from groups, roles via app roles.

plans.name: eSign
plans.notes: Monthly or annual payment; the page does not say which the $25 reflects.

plans.name: Professional
plans.notes: SSO/SAML and API read access are paid add-ons on Professional.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.notes: Includes SSO and API read access; API write access is an add-on.

auth.token_source: Settings > Integrations > SCIM User Provisioning > Settings (Access Token)

endpoints.notes: Inferred from the Entra/Okta feature lists (users and teams); endpoint paths are not published.

operations.notes: Entra lists attribute updates; whether via PUT or PATCH is not stated. A SCIM delete inactivates the user rather than deleting it.

attributes.notes: From the Entra mapping list: userName=email, externalId=Note field, group displayName=Team name.

roles.how: Entra app roles mapped to roles[primary eq "True"].value; Okta user type Administrator, Manager or User.

limitations.text: A user in more than one IdP group gets no team; a GetAccept user can belong to only one team.
Each GetAccept entity needs its own Entra enterprise application.
Okta SCIM can only be set up after SSO is configured.

scim.notes: No page states the SCIM plan. It is recorded on Enterprise because Okta SCIM requires SSO first and SSO is an Enterprise feature (or a paid add-on on Professional). The tenant URL is shown in Settings > Integrations > SCIM User Provisioning and is not published.

auth.notes: Token-based auth or OAuth 2.0 configured by GetAccept Tech Support (the help centre says GetAccept does not issue 'API keys').

limitations.text: API reference is only visible after login; credentials are provisioned by GetAccept.

user_api.notes: API read access is included on Enterprise and an add-on on Professional; API write access is an add-on. The API reference needs a login, so user-management endpoints could not be checked.

okta.notes: Vendor's Okta SCIM guide adds GetAccept from the Okta App Catalog; the OIN page URL was not found (okta.com/integrations/getaccept/ 404). Vendor's separate SSO guide uses a custom SAML app.

entra.notes: Non-gallery enterprise app with the GetAccept SCIM tenant URL and token; no Entra gallery tutorial found.

onelogin.notes: Vendor guide uses OneLogin's SAML Test Connector; no OneLogin provisioning guide. Provisioning false by absence.

fallbacks.notes: SCIM guides are public; the REST API reference requires a login.
